content.user_title: Review UI Accessibility and Visual Design
content.value_statement: Interface reviews can miss accessibility barriers and inconsistent visual details. Rams checks component code against focused WCAG and design criteria with prioritized fixes.
actual_capabilities: Reviews specified component files or asks which files should be assessed.
Identifies missing accessible names, labels, keyboard support, and semantic elements.
Checks focus visibility, heading hierarchy, tab order, and role requirements.
Reviews spacing, typography, contrast, component states, and dark mode consistency.
Prioritizes findings as critical, serious, or moderate with suggested fixes.
Summarizes issue counts and provides a review score.
limitations: Reviews source code and does not test behavior in a browser or assistive technology.
Cannot verify rendered contrast, dimensions, focus order, or runtime state without supporting evidence.
Uses a focused WCAG 2.1 checklist rather than a complete conformance assessment.
Scores are advisory and depend on the files included in the review.

use_cases.title: Audit a new component
use_cases.description: Review a component before release and receive prioritized accessibility fixes.

use_cases.title: Check design consistency
use_cases.description: Find spacing, typography, color, and component state inconsistencies across interface files.

use_cases.title: Prepare an accessibility review
use_cases.description: Identify likely WCAG issues before formal testing and document areas requiring deeper validation.

prompt_templates.title: Review one component
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [component file] for accessibility and visual design issues. Prioritize findings and suggest fixes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single component

prompt_templates.title: Focus on accessibility
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [files] for WCAG 2.1 issues, including names, labels, keyboard access, focus, semantics, and contrast.

prompt_templates.title: Compare related components
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [component files] for inconsistent spacing, typography, states, icon sizing, dark mode, and accessibility behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize release fixes
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [feature files], rank findings by impact, cite lines, propose fixes, and separate verified issues from items needing runtime testing.

output_examples.input: Review the account menu component for accessibility.
output_examples.output: Critical: The icon-only close button lacks an accessible name. Add a concise label. WCAG reference: 4.1.2.

output_examples.input: Check the checkout form for visual and keyboard issues.
output_examples.output: Serious: Focus styling is removed without a visible replacement. Restore a clear focus indicator for keyboard users.

output_examples.input: Compare the loading, disabled, and error states across these buttons.
output_examples.output: Moderate: State styling and icon sizes vary between buttons. Align tokens and preserve distinct text, focus, and disabled cues.

best_practices: Provide complete component files and related styles so findings have sufficient context.
Include the intended framework, design system, and supported browser requirements.
Validate suggested changes with keyboard navigation, browser tools, and assistive technology.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the review score as proof of WCAG conformance.
Do not provide isolated snippets when behavior depends on shared components or styles.
Do not accept automated findings without checking rendered behavior and user impact.

faq.question: What does Rams review?
faq.answer: It reviews component code for selected WCAG 2.1 concerns and visual design consistency.

faq.question: Can it review multiple files?
faq.answer: Yes. Specify the related files, or ask it to locate component files in the project.

faq.question: Does it fix identified issues?
faq.answer: It provides concrete fixes and can apply them when explicitly asked.

faq.question: Does it replace manual accessibility testing?
faq.answer: No. Browser, keyboard, screen reader, zoom, and user testing remain necessary.

faq.question: Which WCAG version does it reference?
faq.answer: Its checklist references WCAG 2.1 criteria for common component accessibility issues.

faq.question: How are findings organized?
faq.answer: Findings are grouped as critical, serious, or moderate, then summarized with counts and an advisory score.
